events.title: Birth
events.summary: Born in Makkah in the year Abrahah's army came against the Ka'bah.

steps.title: Year of the Elephant
steps.summary: Abrahah marches on the Ka'bah with an army and an elephant; Allah destroys them with flocks of birds throwing stones of baked clay.

steps.title: Orphaned young
steps.summary: His father Abdullah dies before he is born; his mother Aminah dies at Abwa when he is about six.

steps.title: Nursed by Halimah
steps.summary: Halimah bint Abi Dhu'ayb of Banu Sa'd takes him to nurse in the desert, the custom for Makkan infants, and her household prospers while he is with her.

steps.title: Abdul Muttalib, then Abu Talib
steps.summary: His grandfather Abdul Muttalib cares for him after Aminah's death, then dies himself two years later; his uncle Abu Talib takes him in and raises him.

events.title: First revelation
events.summary: Jibril comes in the cave of Hira: "Read, in the name of your Lord."

steps.title: Seclusion in Hira
steps.summary: For years before, he goes alone to the cave of Hira to worship, taking food for the stay each time.

steps.title: Iqra
steps.summary: The angel holds him and commands: Read. Three times he says he cannot, until the first verses of Surah al-Alaq come.

steps.title: Khadijah's reassurance
steps.summary: Trembling, he asks to be covered. Khadijah tells him Allah will never disgrace him, for he keeps ties of kinship and helps the weak.

steps.title: Waraqah confirms it
steps.summary: Khadijah's blind Christian cousin Waraqah recognises the description as the same angel sent to Musa, and warns he will be driven out by his own people.

events.title: Makkan revelation
events.summary: The Qur'an that came down before the Hijrah. Every report about a Makkan ayah that names no single event sits here.

steps.title: Three years of secret da'wah
steps.summary: For about three years he calls people privately, one at a time; Khadijah, Abu Bakr, Ali and Zayd are among the first to believe.

steps.title: Warning at Safa
steps.summary: Once commanded to warn his nearest kin, he climbs Safa and calls the clans of Quraysh together to warn them of a severe punishment; Abu Lahab mocks him.

steps.title: Persecution of the weak
steps.summary: Quraysh torture believers who have no clan protection, among them Bilal, and the family of Yasir, whose mother Sumayyah is killed for her faith.

steps.title: The boycott in the valley
steps.summary: Quraysh shut Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib into a valley outside Makkah for about three years, cut off from trade and food, until the pact is torn up.

steps.title: Hamzah and Umar embrace Islam
steps.summary: His uncle Hamzah accepts Islam after Abu Jahl insults the Prophet, and Umar bin al-Khattab, once a fierce opponent, follows soon after; the believers begin to pray openly at the Ka'bah.

events.title: Migration to Abyssinia
events.summary: Persecuted Muslims shelter with the Negus; the last of them return as Khaybar falls.

steps.title: Two waves to Abyssinia
steps.summary: He tells the persecuted believers of a just king across the sea; a small group goes first, then a larger group follows.

steps.title: The first small group
steps.summary: About eleven men and four women slip out of Makkah and cross to Abyssinia, the first hijrah in Islam.

steps.title: Ja'far leads a larger group
steps.summary: A second, larger party of over eighty migrants sets out, led by the Prophet's cousin Ja'far ibn Abi Talib.

steps.title: Quraysh send envoys
steps.summary: Quraysh send Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah with gifts, asking the Negus to hand the migrants back.

steps.title: Ja'far's speech and Surah Maryam
steps.summary: Ja'far describes their old way of life and their new faith, then recites from Surah Maryam about Isa and his mother; the Negus weeps.

steps.title: The Negus refuses to hand them back
steps.summary: Moved by what he hears, the Negus rejects Quraysh's request and returns their gifts, giving the migrants his protection.

steps.title: Return as Khaybar falls
steps.summary: Abu Musa al-Ash'ari's party and Ja'far's group arrive from Abyssinia just as Khaybar is conquered, and the Prophet gives them a share of the spoils.

events.title: Year of Sorrow
events.summary: Khadijah and Abu Talib both die.

steps.title: Khadijah's death
steps.summary: His first wife and closest supporter for twenty-five years dies in Makkah.

steps.title: A house in Paradise
steps.summary: Jibril once told the Prophet to greet Khadijah and give her news of a house in Paradise of reeds, free of noise and hardship.

steps.title: Abu Talib's death
steps.summary: His uncle and protector dies still refusing to say the shahadah, though he shielded the Prophet from Quraysh for years.

steps.title: Quraysh grow bolder
steps.summary: With Khadijah's comfort and Abu Talib's clan protection both gone, Quraysh treat the Prophet more roughly than before.

steps.title: Marriage to Sawdah
steps.summary: He marries Sawdah bint Zam'ah, a widow of an earlier Abyssinia migrant, easing his household's grief.

events.title: Ta'if
events.summary: Rejected and stoned at Ta'if; he makes du'a rather than curse them.

steps.title: Seeking support at Ta'if
steps.summary: He walks to Ta'if to ask the leaders of the tribe of Thaqif for support and protection, since Makkah has grown more hostile.

steps.title: Rejected and stoned
steps.summary: The chiefs of Thaqif refuse him and set their slaves and youths to pelt him with stones until his feet bleed and Zayd bin Harithah is hurt shielding him.

steps.title: Shelter in an orchard
steps.summary: He rests in an orchard belonging to Utbah and Shaybah, sons of Rabi'ah, who send out their Christian slave Addas with a bunch of grapes; Addas recognises the name of Yunus and kisses his hands and feet.

steps.title: The dua at the wall
steps.summary: Alone and hurt, he prays: to You, O Allah, I complain of my weakness and my lack of resources, and my insignificance before people.

steps.title: The hardest day
steps.summary: Aisha later asks if any day was harder than Uhud; he describes this day, when Jibril brought the Angel of the Mountains offering to crush the valley between two mountains, and he declines, hoping their children will worship Allah alone.

steps.title: Jinn hear the Qur'an at Nakhlah
steps.when: On the way back to Makkah
steps.summary: Travelling home, a group of jinn stop to listen to him reciting the Qur'an in the night prayer and return to their people as warners.

events.title: Isra and Mi'raj
events.summary: Night journey to al-Aqsa and ascent through the heavens; the five prayers.

steps.title: Carried on Buraq to Jerusalem
steps.summary: Mounted on Buraq, he travels to Bayt al-Maqdis, ties it at the ring used by the prophets, and prays two rak'ahs inside; Jibril offers him a vessel of wine and one of milk, and he chooses the milk.

steps.title: Chest opened, ascent begins
steps.summary: Jibril opens his chest, washes his heart with Zamzam water, then takes him up through the gates of the seven heavens.

steps.title: Meeting the earlier prophets
steps.summary: He meets Adam, Idris, Musa, Isa and Ibrahim in turn, each greeting him as a righteous prophet and son or brother.

steps.title: Fifty prayers become five
steps.summary: Musa sends him back again and again to ask for less, until five remain, each counted as fifty in reward.

steps.title: The Lote Tree of the utmost boundary
steps.summary: He reaches Sidrat al-Muntaha, wrapped in colours beyond description, and glimpses the greatest signs of his Lord.

events.title: Hijrah
events.summary: Leaves Makkah with Abu Bakr, hides in the cave of Thawr, reaches Madinah.

steps.title: The plot at Dar an-Nadwa
steps.summary: The chiefs of Quraysh meet and settle on a young man from every clan, so no one clan carries the blood.

steps.title: The night of the bed
steps.summary: Ali sleeps in his place under his green cloak while the house is watched.

steps.title: The trusts handed back
steps.summary: Ali is left behind to return what people had left with him for safekeeping, the same people watching the door.

steps.title: Out through the watchers
steps.summary: He leaves the house and goes to Abu Bakr, and the two of them take the road south rather than north.

steps.title: The cave of Thawr
steps.summary: They hide three nights in a cave south of Makkah while the search parties comb the roads.

steps.title: Do not grieve
steps.summary: Abu Bakr sees feet at the mouth of the cave and is told: what do you think of two, the third of whom is Allah.

steps.title: Food carried up at night
steps.summary: Asma bint Abi Bakr brings the provision, tearing her waist-belt in two to tie it, and is named for it after.

steps.title: The day's news brought down
steps.summary: Abdullah ibn Abi Bakr sits among Quraysh by day and carries what is said back to the cave at night; the sheep are driven over the tracks behind him.

steps.title: Suraqah on the road
steps.summary: Suraqah rides them down for the bounty and his horse sinks into the ground under him; he turns back and puts the others off the trail.

steps.title: Quba
steps.summary: He stops at Quba on the edge of the town and a masjid is built there, the first founded upon piety.

steps.title: Entering Madinah
steps.summary: Every household asks him to stay with them; he lets the camel walk on, and builds where it kneels.

events.title: Madinan revelation
events.summary: The Qur'an that came down after the Hijrah. Every report about a Madinan ayah that names no single event sits here.

steps.title: Permission to fight
steps.summary: For the first time permission is given to fight those who make war on the Muslims, after years of ordered patience in Makkah.

steps.title: Qiblah turns to Makkah
steps.summary: Mid prayer at Quba, word comes that the direction of prayer has changed from Jerusalem to the Ka'bah, and the whole row turns together.

steps.title: Wine forbidden in stages
steps.summary: The Qur'an first calls wine a mixed good and a sin, then bars prayer while drunk, then forbids it outright as the work of Satan.

steps.title: Screening verses revealed
steps.summary: Verses come down telling believing women to draw their outer garments close, and setting a screen between the Prophet's wives and other men.

steps.title: The verse on debt
steps.summary: The longest verse in the Qur'an comes down, ordering that loans between people be written down and witnessed.

events.title: Badr
events.summary: About 313 Muslims face a larger Quraysh army and win.

steps.title: Abu Sufyan's caravan
steps.summary: Word reaches Madinah that a large Quraysh trade caravan under Abu Sufyan is coming up from Syria. The Prophet sets out with about three hundred men to intercept it, not meaning to fight a battle.

steps.title: The council of war
steps.summary: The caravan slips past and Quraysh send an army instead. Asked whether to press on, al-Miqdad promises to fight at the Prophet's side wherever he goes.

steps.title: Control of the water
steps.summary: Al-Hubab ibn al-Mundhir suggests moving to the well nearest the enemy and filling in the rest, so the Muslims control the only water on the field. The Prophet accepts the plan.

steps.title: The Prophet's dua
steps.summary: Facing a much larger force, he stretches out his hands and pleads: if this small band is destroyed today, You will not be worshipped on earth.

steps.title: The battle is fought
steps.summary: The two sides meet in single combats before the general fighting starts. Two young Ansari boys, each unaware the other had the same target, cut down Abu Jahl, the leading voice against the Prophet in Makkah.

steps.title: What to do with the captives
steps.summary: Abu Bakr advises ransoming the captives as kin; Umar advises killing them. The Prophet takes Abu Bakr's view, and Allah later reveals a caution about it.

events.title: Uhud
events.summary: The archers leave their post; Hamzah is martyred.

steps.title: The archers leave their post
steps.summary: The Prophet orders fifty archers to hold a hill whatever happens. Seeing what looks like victory, most leave for the spoils, and the battle turns against the Muslims.

steps.title: Hamzah is martyred
steps.summary: Wahshi, promised his freedom, kills Hamzah with a thrown spear. Wahshi later becomes Muslim, and kills the false prophet Musaylimah with the same spear.

steps.title: The Prophet is wounded
steps.summary: His helmet is broken, his face is cut and a tooth is broken. Fatimah washes the wound while Ali pours water, and burnt matting stops the bleeding.

events.title: The Trench
events.summary: The confederates besiege Madinah; a trench is dug; a wind scatters them.

steps.title: Salman's proposal
steps.summary: Salman al-Farisi, who knew Persian siege warfare, suggests digging a trench around the exposed side of Madinah; nothing like it had been used by the Arabs before.

steps.title: A stone against the hunger
steps.summary: Salman finds a rock the spades cannot break. The Prophet strikes it three times, each strike lighting up with a promise of future conquest, though he has tied a stone to his own belly from hunger.

steps.title: The siege tightens
steps.summary: The confederate armies surround Madinah and keep the Muslims so busy defending the trench that they miss the Asr prayer until after sunset.

steps.title: Banu Qurayzah break their pact
steps.summary: Banu Qurayzah, bound by treaty to help defend Madinah, go over to the confederates instead, opening a second front behind the Muslim lines.

steps.title: Single combat with Amr
steps.summary: Amr ibn Abd Wudd, a famed Quraysh warrior, leaps his horse across the trench and challenges the Muslims to single combat. Ali accepts and kills him, and the rest of his party turn back.

steps.title: A wind scatters them
steps.summary: A bitter, cold wind strikes the confederates' camp by night, overturning their tents and cooking pots, and the siege breaks up without a final battle.

events.title: Hudaybiyyah
events.summary: A treaty that looks like a loss and is called a clear victory.

steps.title: Uthman sent to Makkah
steps.summary: The Prophet sends Uthman, well regarded by Quraysh, to tell them he has come only for Umrah. The pledge that follows is taken while he is still away.

steps.title: The pledge under the tree
steps.summary: The Prophet calls the Muslims to pledge to fight if it comes to that. Allah later says He was pleased with them for this pledge.

steps.title: Terms that look like a loss
steps.summary: Suhail insists the words 'Messenger of Allah' be struck from the document, and that anyone who joins the Muslims from Quraysh be returned, but not the reverse.

steps.title: Umar's questions
steps.summary: Umar bin al-Khattab asks why they should accept humbling terms when their cause is true. The Prophet says he will not disobey his Lord, and later events prove him right.

steps.title: Abu Jandal turned back
steps.summary: Abu Jandal arrives dragging his chains, seeking refuge as a new Muslim, but under the treaty's terms Suhail, his own father, takes him back to Makkah.

events.title: Khaybar
events.summary: The fortresses of Khaybar are taken; the emigrants return from Abyssinia.

steps.title: March to Khaybar
steps.summary: The Muslims reach Khaybar's oasis of fortresses by night. At dawn the field workers see the army coming and cry out in alarm.

steps.title: The banner given to Ali
steps.summary: The Prophet promises the banner to a man Allah will grant victory through. He calls for Ali, cures his eye trouble with his own saliva, and hands it to him.

steps.title: The forts fall
steps.summary: Khaybar's fortresses are taken one after another until the Jewish community sues for peace and is allowed to keep working the land for half its produce.

steps.title: The poisoned sheep
steps.summary: A Jewish woman serves the Prophet a roasted sheep laced with poison. He tastes it and stops, and spares her life though he feels its effect afterward.

steps.title: Marriage to Safiyyah
steps.summary: He marries Safiyyah bint Huyay, taken captive at Khaybar. The wedding feast is only dates, dried yoghurt and butter spread on leather sheets.

events.title: Opening of Makkah
events.summary: Makkah is entered almost without fighting; the idols are removed from the Ka'bah.

steps.title: Abu Sufyan sees the army
steps.summary: Abu Sufyan comes out to spy and is caught. He accepts Islam and is placed to watch the Muslim tribes march past in their thousands.

steps.title: Not a day of killing
steps.summary: Sa'd bin Ubada calls it a day when the Ka'bah's sanctity is set aside. The Prophet corrects him: today Allah honours the Ka'bah, and orders it draped in cloth.

steps.title: Whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house
steps.summary: The Prophet announces that whoever enters Abu Sufyan's house, lays down arms, or shuts their own door will be safe.

steps.title: Resistance on Khalid's flank
steps.summary: While the Prophet enters peacefully, Khalid ibn al-Walid's column meets armed resistance entering from Makkah's upper side, and two of his men are killed.

steps.title: The idols are struck down
steps.summary: Three hundred and sixty idols stand around the Ka'bah. The Prophet strikes each with a stick, reciting: truth has come and falsehood has vanished.

events.title: Tabuk
events.summary: A long march in the heat; the hypocrites stay behind.

steps.title: The army of hardship
steps.summary: Unlike other campaigns, the Prophet announces the destination openly this time, because of the summer heat, the distance, and the size of the force ahead.

steps.title: The hypocrites stay behind
steps.summary: Some make excuses not to march and some mock the call to fight in the heat. The Qur'an names their excuses as a test of faith.

steps.title: Ka'b ibn Malik's confession
steps.summary: Ka'b, who stayed behind with no excuse, tells the Prophet the plain truth instead of lying. The believers stop speaking to him and his two companions for fifty days, until the Qur'an announces their forgiveness.

steps.title: No battle at Tabuk
steps.summary: The Byzantine army does not appear. The Prophet takes treaties and tribute from the rulers of Ayla, Dumat al-Jandal and other border towns before returning to Madinah.

events.title: Farewell Hajj
events.summary: The sermon at Arafat; "Today I have perfected your religion for you."

steps.title: The last Hajj announced
steps.summary: After nine years in Madinah without performing Hajj, the Prophet announces he is going, and people come from across Arabia to go with him.

steps.title: The sermon at Arafat
steps.summary: He declares blood and property sacred, ends the blood feuds and usury of pre-Islam, and commands kindness to women, then asks three times: have I conveyed the message?

steps.title: Religion perfected
steps.summary: Allah reveals that the religion is now complete, His favour fulfilled, and Islam confirmed as the faith He has chosen.

steps.title: Stoning and sacrifice
steps.summary: At Mina he stones the largest pillar, sacrifices sixty three camels with his own hand, and performs the farewell circuit of the Ka'bah before leaving Makkah for the last time.

events.title: Death
events.summary: Dies in the room of 'A'ishah; Abu Bakr: "whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died."

steps.title: The illness begins
steps.summary: Growing weak with fever, he asks again and again whether the people have prayed, and asks for water to be poured over him before he can even stand.

steps.title: Abu Bakr leads the prayer
steps.summary: Too weak to lead himself, he orders Abu Bakr to lead the people in prayer, then once comes out leaning on two men and sits beside him while Abu Bakr prays standing.

steps.title: The last siwak
steps.summary: Resting against Aishah's chest, he cleans his teeth with a softened toothstick, then raises his hand and says three times, with the highest companion, before he dies.

steps.title: Abu Bakr's speech
steps.summary: Umar refuses to believe he has died. Abu Bakr tells the people that whoever worshipped Muhammad, Muhammad has died, but whoever worships Allah, Allah is living and never dies, then recites the verse that no messenger lives forever.
